title: Administrators and advisors with a focus on farm animals
description: The county board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to take advantage of the qualities that diversity brings to the business. The rural unit is one of the county board's seven units with approximately 40 employees. The unit is responsible for project and investment support, animal and area-based support, advice and courses for agricultural companies, supervision in agriculture, register checks on animals, land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties and monitoring of basic paid services. Within the unit there is also the Interreg Sweden Norway program for which the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County is the managing authority. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for the agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sector collaboration at the County Board. We work with experts in these fields who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness for the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! The county. This includes, among other things, counseling and skills-enhancing activities aimed at the county's farmers. Our current pet consultant is now retiring and we are therefore looking for her successor who wants to work with skills development for the county's farmers with a focus on the farm's animal husbandry. Job duties You will be part of a group that works with planning, implementing and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy in the form of advice, courses and information to farmers. The work entails partly independently carrying out competence-enhancing initiatives such as courses, counseling and farm meetings with exchange of experience and partly coordinating other actors that the county administrative board has procured for various activities. You write applications for project funds and, together with colleagues, carry out the procurement of competence development efforts. The work includes financial accounting and reporting of measures taken. You collaborate with industry actors and organizations and have close cooperation with other county administrative boards as well as with various functions at our county administrative board. You may be part of cross-sectoral groups where you need to be able to combine your expertise with a holistic perspective. You participate in the work of responding to referrals and contributing with the perspective of agriculture on various issues. Depending on experience and competence, other tasks at the unit may also be part of the position. Your work is independent and requires you to be self-motivated, results-oriented and good at collaborating and creating relationships. You are sensitive to the needs of different clients. In your dialogue with farmers, you need to be service-oriented and have a good understanding of the companies' conditions in the county and have the ability to see the whole. You have a few years of work experience, experience from consultancy and government work is advantageous. You have work experience with a focus on agriculture and farm animals. A particular focus is to • develop the center with support from the steering group and advisory board • ensure the center's progress in line with the operational plan where coordination of sub-activities and utilization of synergies within the center and with other activities is included as a significant part • represent the center in contacts within and outside SLU • work to ensure that the business can be strengthened by, for example, taking initiatives for collaborations with relevant actors and research applications for supplementary funding• work actively for the business's contribution to making a difference for primary producers in Skåne• work for the center's mutual benefit for academia and practice Your manager is the head of unit at the unit for collaboration and development. Your background As an applicant for the position, you must have an academic degree in subject areas relevant to the future development of primary production and related areas. You must have experience of having coordinated collaborations in a leading position and also have worked in or in contact with academic environments. You must have documented leadership experience with financial responsibility. You must be responsive and goal-oriented with an inclusive, communicative and process-oriented way of working. Furthermore, you must be a driven person who is used to working independently while participating in teamwork. Good ability to express oneself verbally and in writing in Swedish and English is a requirement. As networking is an important part of the work, a driver's license is a requirement.  For us, personal suitability is crucial. About us LTV Faculty - Landscape Architecture, Horticulture and Plant Production Science The center has its organizational home at the LTV Faculty. World-leading research in landscape architecture, horticultural science and plant production is conducted here. The faculty offers several educational programs, including the agriculturist program, the horticultural engineering program, and the agroecology program. The LTV faculty is mostly located in Alnarp, in the middle of Sweden's most dynamic agricultural, horticultural and food region. The position will have its operational residence at the unit for collaboration and development in Alnarp. The unit is a cooperation-supporting resource with the task of developing and supporting SLU's internal and external cooperation in order to strengthen the quality and social relevance of SLU's research, education and environmental analysis. Since the cooperation should lead to mutual benefit, the activity should also contribute to knowledge-driven development of companies and relevant organizations in society. At SLU, you take your walk-and-talk meetings and lunchtime walks in the unique Alnarpsparken. Watch the film about our campus at https://www.slu.se/alnarpsfilmen Read more about our benefits and what it's like to work at SLU at https://www.slu.se/om-slu/jobba-pa-slu/ Location: Alnarp Form of employment: Permanent employment. SLU applies 6 month trial employment Scope: 100% or according to agreement Access: According to agreement Application: Welcome with your application via the application button below no later than 2024-10-31. Union contact persons: https://internt.slu.se/min-anstallning/facket/kontaktpersons/ The Swedish University of Agriculture (SLU) has a key role in the development of sustainable living, founded in science and education. Through our focus on the interplay between humans, animals and ecosystems and a responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable social development and good living conditions on our planet. The main locations are Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, but operations are also carried out at research stations, experimental parks and educational locations throughout the country. SLU has just over 3,000 employees, 5,000 students and research students and a turnover of over three billion kroner. The university invests in attractive environments on its campus areas. We work for an equal and inclusive work environment where open conversations between people with different experiences lay the foundation for science, creativity and development. We therefore welcome people with different backgrounds and perspectives to apply for the current position.

input: What other occupations use the last skill you mentioned?
actual_output:
The last skill mentioned in the previous response was **"Lead a team"** (in the context of managing projects and supervising groups). 

Based on the information available in my database, here are several occupations that incorporate the skill of leading and managing teams:

*   **Agricultural scientist:** These professionals plan and implement projects, which often involves leading teams to conduct research on soil, animals, and plants to improve agricultural processes.
*   **Aquaculture hatchery manager:** This role involves directing and coordinating production in large-scale operations. They supervise teams responsible for the breeding, incubation, and early-life rearing stages of fish and shellfish.
*   **Product development manager:** These managers coordinate the development of new products from beginning to end, which requires leading cross-functional teams to balance design, technical requirements, and cost criteria.
*   **Performance lighting designer:** While focused on artistic vision, these designers supervise the execution of their concepts by coaching technical operators and working closely with an entire artistic team.
*   **Sound operator:** Similar to other performance-based roles, these professionals lead the technical execution of a performance by supervising the setup and steering the technical crew to ensure the sound system is operated effectively.
*   **Automated fly bar operator:** This high-risk occupation involves supervising the setup of rigging systems and steering the technical crew to ensure the safe movement of heavy loads during a performance.
*   **Zoo educator:** Depending on the size of the organization, these professionals may lead or coordinate a large team of educators to develop formal and informal learning opportunities for visitors. 

While the context returned by the database does not provide an exhaustive list of every job title in existence, these roles represent the specific occupations identified that involve the coordination and leadership of personnel and projects.

description: Performance lighting designers develop a lighting design concept for a performance and supervise the execution of it. Their work is based on research and artistic vision. Therefore, the designers work closely with artistic directors, operators and the artistic team. During rehearsals and performance, they coach the operators to obtain optimal timing and manipulation. Performance lighting designers develop lighting plots, cue lists and other documentation to support the operators and production crew. They sometimes also work as autonomous artists, creating light art outside a performance context.

Puppet designers make puppets and manipulable objects out of a variety of materials, and may build robotic elements into them. Puppet designers sometimes also work as autonomous artists, creating outside a performance context.

occupation_label: automated fly bar operator
description: Automated fly bar operators control the movements of sets and other elements in a performance based on the artistic or creative concept, in interaction with the performers. Their work is influenced by and influences the results of other operators. Therefore, the operators work closely together with the designers, operators and performers. Automated fly bar operators prepare and supervise the setup, program the equipment and operate automated fly bar systems, rigging systems or systems for horizontal movement. Their work is based on plans, instructions and calculations. The manipulation of heavy loads close to or above performers and audience makes this a high risk occupation.

occupation_label: sound operator
description: Sound operators control the sound of a performance based on the artistic or creative concept, in interaction with the performers. Their work is influenced by and influences the results of other operators. Therefore, the operators work closely together with the designers and performers. They prepare audio fragments, supervise the setup, steer the technical crew, program the equipment and operate the sound system. Their work is based on plans, instructions and other documentation.

occupation_label: product development manager
description: Product development managers coordinate the development of new products from beginning to end. They receive briefings and start envisioning the new product considering design, technical and cost criteria. They conduct research on market needs and create prototypes of new products for untapped market opportunities. Product development managers also improve and boost technological quality.

input: What skills are needed for this occupation?
actual_output:
Based on the information provided from the database for the occupation of **Crisis situation social worker**, the following skills are required:

**Essential Skills:**
*   **Case and Social Management:** Apply case management, plan social service process, organise social work packages, assess social service users' situation, review social service plan, apply decision making within social work, and apply problem solving in social service.
*   **Crisis and Support Intervention:** Apply crisis intervention, manage social crisis, provide social counselling, provide support to social services users, protect vulnerable social service users, contribute to protecting individuals from harm, and build helping relationship with social service users.
*   **Professional Standards and Ethics:** Meet standards of practice in social services, apply quality standards in social services, adhere to organisational guidelines, manage ethical issues within social services, accept own accountability, and undertake continuous professional development in social work.
*   **Social Work Practice:** Social work theory, clinical social work, apply person-centred care, apply holistic approach within social services, promote social change, empower social service users, advocate for social service users, and apply anti-oppressive practices.
*   **Communication and Interpersonal:** Conduct interview in social service, communicate with social service users, negotiate with social service users, listen actively, relate empathetically, and negotiate with social service stakeholders.
*   **Community and Context:** Work within communities, deliver social services in diverse cultural communities, work in a multicultural environment in health care, promote inclusion, and make legislation transparent for users of social services.
*   **Professional Conduct:** Develop professional identity in social work, demonstrate leadership in social service cases, communicate professionally with colleagues in other fields, cooperate at inter-professional level, develop professional network, and address problems critically.
*   **Administrative and General:** Maintain records of work with service users, report on social development, have computer literacy, tolerate stress, manage stress in the work place, apply organisational techniques, and follow health and safety precautions in social care practices.
*   **Legal and Rights:** Legal requirements in the social sector, promote service users' rights, and social justice.

**Optional Skills:**
*   Assess the development of youth
*   Support the positiveness of youths
*   Promote the safeguarding of young people
*   Adolescent psychological development
*   Support children's wellbeing

*   **Foster care support worker:** Assists and supports abused children to recover and ensures their welfare is a priority.
*   **Child welfare worker:** Provides early intervention and support to children and their families to maximize family well-being.
*   **Child day care worker:** Provides social services to children and their families to improve their functioning and maximize well-being.
*   **Residential childcare worker:** Counsels and supports children with physical or mental disabilities in a positive living environment.
*   **Child care coordinator:** Organises child care services and implements care programmes to assist in the development of children.
*   **Early years special educational needs teacher:** Ensures students with disabilities reach their learning potential and addresses their specific needs.
*   **Social pedagogue:** Provides care, support, and education to children and young persons, contributing to their welfare and societal inclusion.
retrieval_context:
occupation: social services manager
description: Social services managers have the responsibility for strategic and operational leadership and management of staff teams and resources within and or across social services. They are responsible for the implementation of legislation and policies relating to, for example, decisions about vulnerable people. They promote social work and social care values and ethics, equality and diversity, and relevant codes guiding practice. They are responsible for liaising with other professionals in criminal justice, education and health. They can be responsible for contributing to local and national policy development.

occupation: academic support officer
description: Academic support officers provide assistance to students with learning problems and act as the main point of contact for these students. They make sure extra tuition and educational programmes are provided to under-represented students with academic or personal issues. They also organise several social activities throughout the academic year.

occupation: educational psychologist
description: Educational psychologists are psychologists employed by educational institutions to provide psychological and emotional support to students in need. They are specialised in the provision of direct support and interventions to students, conducting psychological testing and assessment, and consulting with families, teachers and other school-based student support professionals, such as school social workers and educational counsellors, about the students. They may also work with the school administration to improve practical support strategies in order to improve the students' well-being.

occupation: teacher of talented and gifted students
description: Teachers of talented and gifted students teach students who have strong skills in one or more areas. They monitor the students’ progress, suggest extra activities to stretch and stimulate their skills, introduce them to new topics and subjects, assign homework and grade papers and tests, and finally they provide emotional support when needed. Teachers working with talented and gifted students know how to foster their interest and make them comfortable with their intelligence.

occupation: secondary school teaching assistant
description: Secondary school teaching assistants provide various support services to secondary school teachers such as instructional and practical support. They help with the preparation of lesson materials needed in class and reinforce instructions with students in need of extra attention. They also perform basic clerical duties, monitor the students' learning progress and behaviour and supervise the students with and without the teacher present.

occupation: nanny
description: Nannies provide qualified care services to children on the premises of the employer. They organise play activities and entertain children with games and other cultural and educative activities according to their respective age, prepare meals, give them bathes, transport them from and to school and assist them with homework on a punctual basis.

occupation: educational counsellor
description: Educational counsellors provide practical and emotional support to students in a educational institution, either in small groups, classrooms, or individually. They function as an accessible school official whom students may contact for a wide variety of issues. Educational counsellors may provide advice on personal problems such as social integration and behavioural issues, and on school-related matters such as composing adequate curriculum schedules, discussing test scores, and informing students on further education options. They may work closely with a school social worker and/or school psychologist and make referrals to other support services if necessary.

occupation: early years teaching assistant
description: Early years teaching assistants support the early years teacher in an early years or nursery school. They assist in class instruction, in classroom supervision in absence of the head teacher, and in organising, developing and putting into practice of the daily schedule. Early years teaching assistants monitor and help students in group as well as individually, and tend to focus on the students in need of extra care and attention the early years teacher cannot provide.

occupation: primary school teaching assistant
description: Primary school teaching assistants provide instructional and practical support to primary school teachers. They reinforce instruction with students in need of extra attention and prepare the materials the teacher needs in class. They also perform clerical work, monitor the students' learning progress and behaviour and supervise the students with and without the head teacher present.

occupation: special educational needs assistant
description: Special educational needs assistants assist special education teachers in their classroom duties. They tend to the physical needs of students with a variety of disabilities and help out with tasks such as bathroom breaks, bus rides, eating and classroom switches. They also provide instructional support to students, teachers and parents and prepare lesson programmes. Special educational needs assistants supply support for students tailored to their specific needs, help out with challenging assignments and monitor students' progress and classroom behaviour.

occupation: special educational needs teacher
description: Special educational needs teachers work with and teach children, young people, and adults with an intellectual or physical disability. They use a range of specialised concepts, strategies and tools to optimise learners' communication, mobility, autonomy, and social integration. They select teaching methods and support resources to enable individual learners to maximise their potential for independent living.

occupation: rehabilitation support worker
description: Rehabilitation support workers provide counselling to individuals dealing with birth defects or with major consequences caused by diseases, accidents, and burnouts. They help them to cope with personal, social and vocational issues. They assess the personal needs of clients, develop rehabilitation plans, get involved in the training, and help people undergoing a rehabilitation plan with job placement.

occupation: legal guardian
description: Legal guardians legally assist and support minor children, mentally disabled persons or incapacitated older adults in their personal life. They can manage their property, help with daily financial administration and assist with the ward's medical or social needs.

occupation: child care worker
description: Child care workers provide care for children when the parents or family members are unavailable. They look after the children's basic needs and help or supervise them during play. Child care workers can work for preschools, daycare centres, childcare agencies or individual families.

occupation: adult community care worker
description: Adult community care workers perform assessment and care management of communities of adults who live with physical impairments or convalescing states. They aim to improve their life in the community and enable them to live safely and independently at their own home.

input: Which occupation helps people during emergencies and difficult life situations?
actual_output:
Although there is no information in the database specifically addressing agricultural occupations related to this inquiry, the database provides information regarding a "crisis situation social worker."

A crisis situation social worker provides emergency support and assistance to persons with physical or mental disorders by addressing their distress, impairment, and instability. They are responsible for assessing the level of risk, mobilising client resources, and stabilising the crisis.

input: What skills are essential?
actual_output:
The essential skills for a crisis situation social worker, based on the provided data, are:

*   **Social Justice:** Applying the principles of human rights and social justice on a case-by-case basis.
*   **Apply anti-oppressive practices:** Identifying oppression and enabling service users to improve their lives and environment.
*   **Provide social counselling:** Assisting and guiding users to resolve personal, social, or psychological difficulties.
*   **Social work theory:** Understanding theories underpinned by social sciences and humanities.
*   **Involve service users and carers in care planning:** Evaluating care needs and involving families in support plans.
*   **Work within communities:** Establishing social projects for community development.
*   **Meet standards of practice in social services:** Practicing in a lawful, safe, and effective way.
*   **Empower social service users:** Enabling individuals and communities to gain control over their lives.
*   **Apply quality standards in social services:** Upholding social work values while applying quality standards.
*   **Apply case management:** Assessing, planning, coordinating, and advocating for services on behalf of a person.
*   **Apply problem solving in social service:** Using a systematic, step-by-step process to provide services.
*   **Apply crisis intervention:** Responding methodologically to disruptions in the normal functioning of a person, family, or community.
*   **Legal requirements in the social sector:** Understanding prescribed legislative and regulatory requirements.
*   **Protect vulnerable social service users:** Providing support in dangerous situations and removing users to safety.
*   **Contribute to protecting individuals from harm:** Reporting dangerous, abusive, or discriminatory behavior.
*   **Develop professional identity in social work:** Understanding the professional framework and the specific needs of clients.
*   **Provide support to social services users:** Helping users identify strengths and make informed decisions.
*   **Deliver social services in diverse cultural communities:** Being mindful of different cultural traditions and human rights policies.
*   **Social sciences:** Applying sociological, anthropological, and psychological theories.
*   **Conduct interview in social service:** Exploring a client's experiences, attitudes, and opinions.
*   **Demonstrate leadership in social service cases:** Taking the lead in the practical handling of cases.
*   **Communicate professionally with colleagues in other fields:** Cooperating with other professionals in health and social services.
*   **Follow health and safety precautions in social care practices:** Ensuring hygienic and safe environments.
*   **Plan social service process:** Defining objectives, identifying resources, and establishing evaluation indicators.
*   **Promote social change:** Taking into account unpredictable changes at micro, macro, and mezzo levels.
*   **Advocate for social service users:** Speaking on behalf of less advantaged users.
*   **Prevent social problems:** Implementing actions to enhance the quality of life for all citizens.
*   **Make legislation transparent for users of social services:** Explaining legislative implications to users.
*   **Negotiate with social service users:** Building trust and encouraging cooperation.
*   **Promote service users' rights:** Supporting a client's right to control their life and make informed choices.
*   **Apply person-centred care:** Putting individuals at the heart of all decisions.
*   **Clinical social work:** Assessing, diagnosing, and treating bio-psychological problems and behavioral disturbances.
*   **Assess social service users' situation:** Balancing curiosity and respect while identifying needs, resources, and risks.
*   **Crisis intervention:** Utilizing coping strategies to help individuals overcome problems and avoid psychological breakdown.
*   **Relate empathetically:** Recognizing and sharing the emotions and insights of others.
*   **Listen actively:** Giving full attention to others and providing solutions accordingly.
*   **Manage social crisis:** Responding to social crises in a timely manner using available resources.
*   **Manage ethical issues within social services:** Applying ethical principles to resolve dilemmas.
*   **Review social service plan:** Following up on plans while considering user feedback.
*   **Apply decision making within social work:** Making decisions within the limits of authority while considering user input.
*   **Adhere to organisational guidelines:** Understanding and following organizational standards and motives.
*   **Apply holistic approach within social services:** Recognizing connections between different dimensions of social problems and policies.
*   **Work in a multicultural environment in health care:** Interacting with individuals from various cultures.
*   **Address problems critically:** Identifying strengths and weaknesses in approaches to formulate solutions.
*   **Apply socially just working principles:** Working in accordance with human rights and organizational values.
*   **Promote inclusion:** Preventing discrimination and ensuring a positive environment.
*   **Maintain records of work with service users:** Keeping accurate and timely records while complying with privacy legislation.
*   **Develop professional network:** Reaching out to others in a professional context for mutual benefit.
*   **Negotiate with social service stakeholders:** Dealing with institutions, employers, and landlords to achieve the best result for the client.
*   **Report on social development:** Presenting results and conclusions in an intelligible way.
*   **Undertake continuous professional development in social work:** Updating knowledge and skills within one's scope of practice.
*   **Have computer literacy:** Utilizing modern IT equipment and technology.
*   **Tolerate stress:** Maintaining effective performance under pressure.
*   **Apply organisational techniques:** Employing procedures to facilitate goals and manage schedules.
*   **Refer social service users:** Making referrals to other professionals or organizations based on needs.
*   **Organise social work packages:** Creating support services according to regulations and timescales.
*   **Communicate with social service users:** Using various communication methods tailored to the user's needs and culture.
*   **Consider social impact of actions on service users:** Considering the political and cultural context of actions.
*   **Cooperate at inter-professional level:** Working with people in other sectors.
*   **Company policies:** Understanding the rules governing organizational activity.
*   **Accept own accountability:** Recognizing the limits of one's own scope of practice.
*   **Manage stress in the work place:** Coping with professional and institutional stress to avoid burnout.
*   **Build helping relationship with social service users:** Fostering trust through authentic, empathetic, and caring interaction.

input: Are there any open positions related to that occupation?
actual_output:
Based on the information provided in the database, there are no open positions listed for a "crisis situation social worker."

However, the database does contain information about currently open positions within the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County related to agricultural and rural administration. These include:

*   **Administrators and advisors with a focus on farm animals:** This role involves planning and implementing skills development for farmers (advice, courses, and farm meetings), coordinating actors, and handling project fund applications.
*   **Chef till funktionen Jordbrukarstöd (Manager for the Agricultural Support function):** A leadership position responsible for managing 10–15 employees who handle animal and area-based support, register checks on animals, and land acquisition permits.
*   **Säsongsarbetare till Vattenenheten (Seasonal workers for the Water Unit):** Positions focused on field operations for water and fishery conservation, such as restoring watercourses, manual restoration of streams, and inventory work. 

While these roles do not match the occupation of a social worker, some positions—specifically those at the County Administrative Board—note that the work may include "service in crisis staff" as part of the employment requirements.

title: Administrators and advisors with a focus on farm animals
description: The county board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to take advantage of the qualities that diversity brings to the business. The rural unit is one of the county board's seven units with approximately 40 employees. The unit is responsible for project and investment support, animal and area-based support, advice and courses for agricultural companies, supervision in agriculture, register checks on animals, land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties and monitoring of basic paid services. Within the unit there is also the Interreg Sweden Norway program for which the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County is the managing authority. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for the agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sector collaboration at the County Board. We work with experts in these fields who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness for the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! The county. This includes, among other things, counseling and skills-enhancing activities aimed at the county's farmers. Our current pet consultant is now retiring and we are therefore looking for her successor who wants to work with skills development for the county's farmers with a focus on the farm's animal husbandry. Job duties You will be part of a group that works with planning, implementing and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy in the form of advice, courses and information to farmers. The work entails partly independently carrying out competence-enhancing initiatives such as courses, counseling and farm meetings with exchange of experience and partly coordinating other actors that the county administrative board has procured for various activities. You write applications for project funds and, together with colleagues, carry out the procurement of competence development efforts. The work includes financial accounting and reporting of measures taken. You collaborate with industry actors and organizations and have close cooperation with other county administrative boards as well as with various functions at our county administrative board. You may be part of cross-sectoral groups where you need to be able to combine your expertise with a holistic perspective. You participate in the work of responding to referrals and contributing with the perspective of agriculture on various issues. Depending on experience and competence, other tasks at the unit may also be part of the position. Your work is independent and requires you to be self-motivated, results-oriented and good at collaborating and creating relationships. You are sensitive to the needs of different clients. In your dialogue with farmers, you need to be service-oriented and have a good understanding of the companies' conditions in the county and have the ability to see the whole. You have a few years of work experience, experience from consultancy and government work is advantageous. You have work experience with a focus on agriculture and farm animals. If you also have experience in project management and work with skills development, as well as experience in working with small business owners, this is advantageous. You have the ability to communicate clearly in both speech and writing and have an established network within the agricultural industry. You are structured and solution-oriented with good computer skills. The position involves travel, mainly in the county, but longer trips with overnight stays also occur. A driver's license for a passenger car is required. We offer you meaningful work with varied tasks. You will make a difference to our county and society. The County Board is a broad authority, which means that you constantly have the opportunity to develop and learn new things. This applies in several policy areas. As an employer, we have a strong focus on good employment conditions, active work environment work and health-promoting wellness activities. We are keen on cooperation with our union partners and can offer remote work. In case of permanent employment at the County Board, you will be placed at war with the authority. Depending on the service, this may include serving in crisis staff and security classification. We usually start with trial employment for permanent positions. You can find information about how we process your personal data at www.lansstyrelsen.se/dataskydd

title: Säsongsarbetare till Vattenenheten
description: The County Administrative Board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to safeguard the qualities that diversity adds the business. At the water unit, more than 30 employees work. Here we work broadly with issues regarding water, fishing and environmental monitoring in the county. Everything from restoration of aquatic environments, liming and fishing to water management, environmental analysis and drinking water supply. The unit also runs its own water laboratory, which in turn is a central role in the county administrative boards' work with calke power follow -up. The water unit is constantly working to increase the pace of action and the action setting in the county partly by communicating contributions to local water conservation projects and fishing projects through fishing care grants, and partly by seeking new water conservation projects within the EU's various environmental and fisheries funds. At the unit, experts work who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness to the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! Description we are looking for committed people who are interested in working with water and fishery care at the County Administrative Board I Jämtland County during the summer season 2025. The work focuses on improving the habitats for fish, river pearl mussel, otters and other aquatic species in the county's water. If you share our passion to promote and preserve the biodiversity in our aquatic environments, we look forward to your application. We are looking for about 15-20 people for the field operations linked to our long-term work with water and fisheries. The work is largely done in ongoing restoration projects, such as the EU projects Rivers of Life and Ecostreams for Life but also in other assignments linked to water conservation and fishing. The services may vary in time from about 3-6 months. Most of the work takes place in the field between June and October. Some of the services may be relevant to start earlier and completed later and contain more administrative tasks. A significant portion of the tasks are performed in a place other than the place of employment Östersund, which means that overnight stays elsewhere may be required, sometimes during a whole work week. The opportunities for holidays are limited. Work tasks have been primarily to participate in the field operations. Preparations, data settlement and compilations of field work performed can also be included. Other business -related tasks may also be relevant. Each service may include one or more of the following tasks:- Plan and lead the work on restoring watercourses, which is done together with excavator drivers in a team. - Action inventory of fleet -cleaned watercourses with the support of Esris applications Survey and Field Maps. - Manual restoration of streams. - Manually construct play areas for fish in watercourses. - Dust extracts. - Inventory and restoration of ditched wetlands. - Electric test fishing, web test fishing, cancer test fishing in lakes and streams. - Hiking obstacle inventory of older ponds and road crossings. - Conduct chainsaw and clearing work. Enter the date in the application when you can start and how long you can work. We value these properties highly. You must master the Swedish language in speech and writing. We strive for an equal working environment. To perform the work you need to have good field experience, be physically equipped to spend all days in forest and land, wade in running water, work from boat and carry field equipment to and from watercourses. The work includes trips within the county, which means that B-driving license is a requirement. Extra merit for the service is if you have science education with relevant focus and/or experience in field work in the areas included in the tasks, especially task 1, 2, 3 And 7.Andr merit qualifications include a strong interest in water conservation, fishing care and nature conservation. We will process applications and initiate interviews on an ongoing basis.We offer you meaningful work with varied tasks. You will make a difference for our county and society. input: I want to work on sustainable energy solutions. Which occupation would fit me?
actual_output:
Based on the available information from the database, there are numerous occupations focused on sustainable energy solutions. Depending on your specific interest in design, maintenance, consulting, or sales, you might consider the following roles:

*   **Engineering & Design:**
    *   **Renewable energy engineer:** Researches alternative energy sources and designs systems to optimize production and reduce environmental strain.
    *   **Energy engineer:** Designs new, efficient, and clean ways to produce and distribute energy, focusing on sustainability.
    *   **Solar energy engineer:** Designs systems to generate electricity from sunlight.
    *   **Onshore wind energy engineer:** Designs, installs, and maintains wind energy farms.
    *   **Offshore renewable energy engineer:** Manages the installation and design of offshore energy farms and tests equipment like wave and tidal generators.
    *   **Alternative fuels engineer:** Designs systems and motors that use renewable/non-fossil fuels like biodiesel, biomass, or hydrogen.
    *   **Hydropower engineer:** Plans and designs facilities that generate electricity from the movement of water.
    *   **Electric power generation engineer:** Develops systems for electrical power generation with a focus on sustainable and efficient solutions.
    *   **Energy systems engineer:** Supervises energy conversion and distribution, focusing on improving efficiency and integrating renewable energy.

*   **Consulting & Analysis:**
    *   **Energy consultant:** Advises clients on energy sources and how to reduce their carbon footprint.
    *   **Renewable energy consultant:** Provides specialized advice on the advantages of different renewable energy sources.
    *   **Energy manager:** Coordinates energy use within an organization to implement sustainability policies and minimize environmental impact.
    *   **Energy analyst:** Evaluates energy consumption in buildings and recommends cost-effective, efficient alternatives.
    *   **Energy assessor:** Determines energy performance for buildings and advises on energy conservation.
    *   **Energy conservation officer:** Promotes energy conservation and enforces efficiency improvements in homes and businesses.

*   **Technical & Sales Support:**
    *   **Hydropower technician:** Installs and maintains hydropower plant systems.
    *   **Geothermal technician:** Installs and maintains geothermal power and heating installations.
    *   **Renewable energy sales representative:** Promotes renewable energy products and secures sales for renewable energy suppliers.
    *   **Solar energy sales consultant:** Advises clients on solar energy to promote it as a sustainable alternative.

j.title: Expert/project manager in milk for sustainable animal production
j.description: Do you have knowledge of and experience in milk production? Do you want to work with the sustainable milk production of the future together with companies and the consultancy in the agricultural and animal sector? Then this could be a service for you! About us The government wishes to strengthen competitiveness in animal production for food by ensuring that the newest knowledge nationally and internationally is useful for Swedish producers. Knowledge hub animal production is a new unit within RISE that we are building together with experts in the field and who have competence in knowledge transfer, advice and communication. Together with the actors, we will identify the needs of animal production and develop models and advisory methods, which will put the knowledge to use by the farmer. The knowledge hub should not conduct research or advice itself, but be a link between the research and the advice and should collect knowledge from different areas and make it useful for advisory companies and the farmers. About the role We are now expanding our team with another expert in the field of milk production. As an expert in our team, you get the opportunity to work with acquisition, compilation and transfer of knowledge regarding milk production, animal health and welfare, breeding, feed, milk quality, new technology and entrepreneurship. This is for a future sustainable Swedish animal production, which contributes to good animal welfare and working environment, together with good profitability. You will be an important team player in a committed department with high competence and who values ​​working in close collaboration with both colleagues within RISE and with our partners. You will have an important key role where you gather and coordinate different competences in milk production with our experts, industry partners and other RISE competencies, to contribute to knowledge transfer based on the animal producer's current and future needs. The position is located in Uppsala or Lund and involves some travel, therefore a B driving license is a requirement. Who are you? You have experience and knowledge of the entire milk production process, i.e. knowledge within i.a. animal health, breeding, feed, production economics and management. We would like you to have experience of working interdisciplinary, as well as working with information delivery and identifying farmers' knowledge needs, in national/international projects. It is advantageous if you have several years of work experience in the field of milk production, information efforts/further training and counseling for agricultural entrepreneurs. As a person, you are focused, committed, driven and good at building relationships with e.g. You work goal-oriented and structured and have a strong ability to quickly absorb information and events. Your way of thinking is strategic and you have a good overall view. You are proactive and systematic in your way of working and like to think new things. Very good knowledge of Swedish and English, both spoken and written, is a requirement. What do we offer you? With us at RISE, you will get to work with an incredibly broad and exciting business. You will be part of a network of experts where you will be given the opportunity to exchange experience and develop skills as well as a valuable sounding board. You will collaborate with our researchers and experts in agricultural production. The culture is characterized by a positive spirit where everything is possible and where we work focused towards our common goals. You will work in a dynamic environment that gives you development opportunities both professionally and personally. j.title: Phd position within Sustainable Feed for Poultry and Pigs
j.description: Department of Applied Animal Science and WelfareThe goal at our institution is to promote good animal husbandry and animal welfare as well as sustainable food production with high product quality. We do this through research and education on animals with a focus on feed and nutrition, management and the environment, ethology, animal ethics and animal welfare. We are about 125 employees working in Uppsala, Skara, Umeå and Gothenburg.As a PhD student, you will be in a creative and stimulating environment with the opportunity to network with both the business community and international contacts.More information about the department: Department of Applied Animal Science and Welfare.Read more about our benefits and what it is like to work at SLU at https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/work-at-slu/Research project: Sustainable feed for poultry and pigsResearch subject: Animal ScienceDescription:Department of Applied Animal Science and Welfare, Lantmännen and the competence centre SustAinimal work together to explore the role of livestock for future increased, sustainable and competitive food production in Sweden. Focus is profitable solutions delivering food and ecosystem services in various parts of the food sector.In Swedish poultry and pig production, feed accounts for the majority of both the production costs and the global warming potential. The animals' feed conversion ratio and the choice of feed ingredients thus have a significant impact on the production's climate impact. In addition to the climate impact, contributions to biodiversity, circularity, competition between feed and food, and self-sufficiency are important sustainability parameters. Future animal production needs feed that can meet these upcoming challenges without losing profitability and competitiveness. Possible strategies could include a higher proportion of feed ingredients produced from side streams and materials unsuitable for human consumption.This project aims to develop and evaluate new feed compositions with the goal of reduced environmental impact, increased self-sufficiency, and increased use of feed ingredients produced from side streams, all while maintaining good profitability.Work tasks: The work involves planning, organizing, and doing practical work while conducting animal trials at SLU's research facility Swedish Livestock Research Centre. The tasks also include compiling, statistically analyzing, and publishing results from the conducted studies, as well as working with databases and sustainability assessments.As a doctoral student, the responsibilities includes oral presentations and written publications of the project in scientific and popular science contexts. The doctoral student is also expected to participate in teaching activities at both undergraduate and advanced levels.Qualifications:At the time of employment, a degree at advanced level is required for the position. We are looking for a candidate with a degree in Agricultural Science, a Master's degree in Animal Science, Biology, or another relevant field. You must also have documented good knowledge in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Swedish or other Nordic languages is considered an advantage. A driver's license for car is also an advantage.Previous experience in statistical data analysis, working with databases and sustainability assessments, strong computer skills, and working with pigs or poultry and their feeding is considered advantageous. j.title: Business manager for the new center for sustainable primary production
j.description: The unit for cooperation and development Do you want to take a key role in the development of knowledge for a sustainable primary production of food? Through an investment in the future, in collaboration between Sparbanken Skåne and SLU, this knowledge center is now being established, which will take advantage of Skåne's excellent conditions for sustainable food production through knowledge, innovation and new technical opportunities in collaboration between academia and the agricultural and horticultural industries. We are now looking for you to lead the center's development from the start, in close collaboration with SLU's research and education and with the support of management functions. You will be the operative spider in the network to take advantage of synergies and secure progress in the business. Read more in SLU's press release: 50 million invested in new knowledge center for sustainable food production in Alnarp | Externwebben (slu.se) About the job SLU and Sparbanken Skåne's center for sustainable primary production The formation of the center will promote sustainable primary production and work for a robust food chain that benefits economic growth and development in Scania in the long term. Through outstanding research and education, the center will collaborate with business and public actors to develop, disseminate and utilize knowledge and new solutions for a transition that balances economic, ecological and social sustainability. The center has four overarching goal areas for the operation.• Increased knowledge and innovation for increased sustainability in primary production• Increased collaboration in research and development• Higher level of technology in research, education and industry• Strengthen Skåne's contribution to the development of primary production in Sweden The center shall contribute to creating collaborations in order to make use of competence and resources which, in the long run, lead to even more results in primary production companies and in research and education. Duties Your area of ​​responsibility as business manager is to, in dialogue with management functions, be responsible for the centre's whole and sub-projects and to be the contact person towards Sparbanken Skåne and other partners to ensure business progress and goal achievement. A particular focus is to • develop the center with support from the steering group and advisory board • ensure the center's progress in line with the operational plan where coordination of sub-activities and utilization of synergies within the center and with other activities is included as a significant part • represent the center in contacts within and outside SLU • work to ensure that the business can be strengthened by, for example, taking initiatives for collaborations with relevant actors and research applications for supplementary funding• work actively for the business's contribution to making a difference for primary producers in Skåne• work for the center's mutual benefit for academia and practice Your manager is the head of unit at the unit for collaboration and development. Your background As an applicant for the position, you must have an academic degree in subject areas relevant to the future development of primary production and related areas. You must have experience of having coordinated collaborations in a leading position and also have worked in or in contact with academic environments. You must have documented leadership experience with financial responsibility. You must be responsive and goal-oriented with an inclusive, communicative and process-oriented way of working. Furthermore, you must be a driven person who is used to working independently while participating in teamwork. Good ability to express oneself verbally and in writing in Swedish and English is a requirement. As networking is an important part of the work, a driver's license is a requirement.  For us, personal suitability is crucial. About us LTV Faculty - Landscape Architecture, Horticulture and Plant Production Science The center has its organizational home at the LTV Faculty. World-leading research in landscape architecture, horticultural science and plant production is conducted here. The faculty offers several educational programs, including the agriculturist program, the horticultural engineering program, and the agroecology program. The LTV faculty is mostly located in Alnarp, in the middle of Sweden's most dynamic agricultural, horticultural and food region. The position will have its operational residence at the unit for collaboration and development in Alnarp. The unit is a cooperation-supporting resource with the task of developing and supporting SLU's internal and external cooperation in order to strengthen the quality and social relevance of SLU's research, education and environmental analysis. Since the cooperation should lead to mutual benefit, the activity should also contribute to knowledge-driven development of companies and relevant organizations in society. At SLU, you take your walk-and-talk meetings and lunchtime walks in the unique Alnarpsparken. Watch the film about our campus at https://www.slu.se/alnarpsfilmen Read more about our benefits and what it's like to work at SLU at https://www.slu.se/om-slu/jobba-pa-slu/ Location: Alnarp Form of employment: Permanent employment. SLU applies 6 month trial employment Scope: 100% or according to agreement Access: According to agreement Application: Welcome with your application via the application button below no later than 2024-10-31. Union contact persons: https://internt.slu.se/min-anstallning/facket/kontaktpersons/ The Swedish University of Agriculture (SLU) has a key role in the development of sustainable living, founded in science and education. Through our focus on the interplay between humans, animals and ecosystems and a responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable social development and good living conditions on our planet. The main locations are Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, but operations are also carried out at research stations, experimental parks and educational locations throughout the country. SLU has just over 3,000 employees, 5,000 students and research students and a turnover of over three billion kroner. The university invests in attractive environments on its campus areas. We work for an equal and inclusive work environment where open conversations between people with different experiences lay the foundation for science, creativity and development. We therefore welcome people with different backgrounds and perspectives to apply for the current position.

j.title: Chef till funktionen Jordbrukarstöd
j.description: The County Administrative Board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to safeguard the qualities that diversity adds the business. The country countryside unit is one of the County Administrative Board's seven units with approximately 40 employees. The unit is responsible for project and investment support, animal and area-based support, advice and courses for agricultural companies, supervision in agriculture, register checks on animals, land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties and monitoring of basic payment services. Within the unit there is also Interreg Sweden the Norway program for which the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County is the managing authority. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sectoral cooperation on the county administrative board. With us, experts work in these areas who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness to the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! Descriptions The newly formed function of agricultural support we are now looking for a manager. The function consists of between 10 -15 Employees depending on the season and work mainly with handling and control of animal and area-based support for agriculture, register checks on animals and land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties. The function also participates in cross -sectoral collaborations on the county administrative board and acts as experts when answering referrals and when preparing various issues linked to the county's agriculture. Work tasks as a function manager will be your role to lead the work based on our assignment and in accordance with the county administrative board's overall priorities. In daily work, you are a present manager who practices a trust -based leadership to create a good workplace for your employees and colleagues. You have target and results responsibility for the function and work closely with the unit manager and deputy unit manager on issues related to financial follow-up and strategic planning. You are part of the unit's management team and together with other managers take overall responsibility for the unit's operations and development. Collaborations with other function managers on the county administrative board and in cross -sectoral working groups are a natural part of your work. In addition to your managerial assignment you will also work with other tasks that are included in the operation of the function or unit. Depending on your background and competence, the data may vary but will constitute approximately 50% of your working hours. Qualification you have college education in an area relevant to the service, for example as an agronomist or surveyor or other education that the employer considers equivalent. You have experience of personnel management and being manager and leader and are confident in that role. Furthermore, you have knowledge and experience of issues related to agriculture and food production and a good understanding of the conditions that apply to Swedish agriculture. If you have experience in support management or work at the authority, it is a merit. You are a responsive manager who is good at listening and who can create commitment to your employees. You communicate and handle any conflicts in a constructive way, are loyal to your mission and have a positive attitude towards your work.  You can weigh complex information and show judgment in statements, actions and decisions. The work requires that you are structured and can plan, organize and prioritize in an appropriate way, you set up and keep time frames for your work. In order to succeed in the role, it is important to be able to collaborate with both people on the unit and other units and to be able to see whole and take into account a larger perspective. We offer you meaningful work with varied tasks. You will make a difference for our county and society. The County Administrative Board is a broad authority, which means that you are constantly being given the opportunity to develop and learn new things. This applies in several policy areas. As an employer, we have a great focus on good employment conditions, active work environment work and health promotion wellness activities. We care about collaboration with our trade union parties and can offer distance work. Depending on service, it may include service in crisis staff and security rating. We usually start with probationary employment at permanent services.information on how we process your personal data can be found at www.lansstyrelsen.se/datasktkt

input: What other occupations require the last skill you mentioned?
actual_output:
The skill referred to in your previous request is **"Promote sustainable energy"** (identified by ID `http://data.europa.eu/esco/skill/0e81fcff-2fb5-4c87-afc2-49b5e5d9db50`).

According to the provided database, the following occupations require this skill:

*   **Anaerobic digestion plant operator:** They oversee and maintain the process of breaking down organic matter (such as food waste) in the absence of oxygen to produce biogas. Their responsibilities include monitoring performance, troubleshooting issues, and conducting regular inspections of the process.
*   **Biogas technician:** They work in the derivation of gas from organic matter (produced as landfill gas or digested gas). Their tasks include operating equipment in biogas plants, performing tests, carrying out maintenance, and taking action in the event of system failures.
